articles.title: New Israel parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot works to form new govt
articles.description: Israel's new parliament will be sworn on Tuesday, November 10, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu set to lose his majority as rival Gadi Eisenkot works to form a new government. The opposition hopes to use its newfound legislative power to move quickly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky has more.

related.title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot prepares government
related.description: Israel's new parliament is set to be sworn in Tuesday with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's camp holding a majority. Eisenkot seeks to build a coalition after receiving a mandate to form a government.

articles.title: US Hegseth faces Republican impeachment bid over abuse of power in Iran war
articles.description: A Republican lawmaker moved on Monday to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting the stage for a potentially explosive vote in Congress, days after President Donald Trump's party suffered a crushing defeat in the midterms. Kentucky Congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment, accusing Hegseth of waging war illegally without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

articles.title: US Republican Thomas Massie launches bid to impeach Pete Hegseth
articles.description: US Republican Thomas Massie moved Monday, November 9, to force a vote to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing his fellow Republicans to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses blamed in part on fallout from the war in Iran. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Washington Fraser Jackson has more.

articles.title: Live: US envoy urges new security framework to secure peace in Ukraine amid trilateral talks
articles.description: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States began their first trilateral talks in more than nine months in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, as Washington seeks to broker an end to the war and Kyiv faces pressure over territorial concessions. articles.title: Dana White: UFC chief declines Trump’s White House job offer
articles.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White made a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday to turn down Donald Trump’s offer of a job as the White House press secretary, saying he has “zero political aspirations”. Trump stunned the world on November 7 when he said on social media that he had offered White the job, only to claim a day later that he was "only kidding”.

articles.title: California voters reject measure to tax the wealth of billionaires
articles.description: California voters have rejected a first-in-the-nation tax on the net worth of billionaires following a contentious ballot fight that generated huge spending by some prominent tech leaders eager to stop their taxes from going up. The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Los Angeles Loic Pialat has more.

articles.title: En Pologne, les démocrates ont besoin de l’unité de l’Europe
articles.description: Alors que la violence saisit une société polonaise très divisée, les Européens doivent serrer les rangs autour du premier ministre de centre droit, Donald Tusk. Les démocraties auraient tout à craindre de la perspective d’un retour au pouvoir du PiS, allié à l’extrême droite.

articles.title: Les îles du Pacifique, aux avant-postes de la lutte contre le changement climatique, veulent se faire entendre à la COP31
articles.description: Aux avant-postes de la lutte contre le changement climatique, les îles du Pacifique sont, avec la Turquie et l’Australie, le troisième acteur de la COP31, qui s’est ouverte lundi à Antalya dans une configuration inédite.

articles.description: A recent Greek National Opera production afforded a group of seniors the chance to channel their young-at-heart energy into onstage performances, proving that no one's too old to learn something new. It challenged the premise that retirement means surrendering to a sedentary lifestyle and extinguishing one’s creative spirit.

articles.title: Peru gets ready to welcome Pope Leo XIV on his South America tour
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV continued his South American tour on Wednesday, November 11, with a visit to Peru, after stops in Uruguay and Argentina. The American-born pontiff lived in Peru for several years and even became a Peruvian citizen. Ahead of his arrival, the country unveiled a giant statue in his honour.

articles.title: China's 'impossible to ignore' tech rise on display at Web Summit in Lisbon
articles.description: One of Europe's biggest annual tech events, the Web Summit, kicked off in the Portuguese capital this week with the biggest ever delegation of Chinese business leaders and policymakers. FRANCE 24's Charles Pellegrin talks to Dr. Dan Wang, China Director at Eurasia Group, about EU-China tech relations, the climate of suspicion created by the spying scandal at Nvidia, and what the EU's quest for tech sovereignty could mean for China.

articles.title: En France, 659 morts liées à la consommation de drogues ou de médicaments en 2024, une hausse de 171 % en dix ans
articles.description: Les médicaments de substitution restent « la première cause de surdose en France », avec, en 2024, « 338 décès, soit 51 % des cas », suivis par la cocaïne (222 décès), l’héroïne (75), le cannabis (65), les amphétamines dont le MDMA (41) et les nouveaux produits de synthèse (33), dont les cathinones et les nitazènes.

articles.title: Inspiring Senegal's next generation: Free tickets bring children to Dakar 2026
articles.description: As part of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, 200,000 free tickets will be distributed to schools and community organisations. The aim is to give as many young people as possible the chance to experience the Games. FRANCE 24’s team on the ground reports.

articles.title: Ugandan former intelligence officer exposes alleged army abuses
articles.description: In Uganda, a former military intelligence officer accused the army of secretly detaining and torturing opponents in clandestine houses. In late September, Lieutenant Herbert Matanda Mabonga released videos that sparked an outcry in the country and were widely shared on social media. FRANCE 24 correspondent in the region spoke with him from his place of exile.
